newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pollster says Kohl well placed for 1998 reelection.
newsitem.headline: Pollster says Kohl well placed for 1998 reelection.

text.p: The German pollster who regularly gives Helmut Kohl his lowest ratings said on Wednesday the veteran chancellor stood a good chance of reversing current trends and winning reelection in September 1998.

Manfred Guellner, head of the Forsa polling company, wrote in the Die Woche weekly that Kohl's current low popularity ratings were not so threatening because many supporters of his Christian Democratic Union (CDU) were still undecided.

By contrast, the opposition SPD's strong showing in the polls could fade next year because neither of its two possible candidates -- party leader Oskar Lafontaine or Lower Saxony state premier Gerhard Schroeder -- has a solid following.
"So Helmut Kohl can be quite relaxed, despite the bad poll results for the CDU," Guellner wrote. "If the SPD does not really change, he has a good chance to be reelected in 1998."

Forsa's latest weekly poll for Die Woche gave the CDU and its Bavarian CSU sister party only 34 percent compared to 40 percent for the SPD. Kohl's Free Democrat (FDP) coalition partner scored only six percent while the SPD's probable partner, the Greens, got 11 percent support.

Forsa's surveys have for months been showing Kohl's CDU running slightly lower and the SPD higher than other major German polls. Pollsters say this depends on the mathematical formulae used to evaluate raw data.
Guellner said a high 31 percent of Germans were currently undecided and one third of them were CDU voters Kohl could win back next year as he did in 1994.
"The current political situation resembles the start of the 1994 'super election year', when a large part of the undecided voters were dissatisfied CDU supporters," he wrote.
"The SPD would be well advised to evaluate their current favourable poll results realistically," he added.
Guellner said most Germans felt Lafontaine, the failed SPD challenger in 1990, was not qualified to be chancellor and only half of the SPD voters surveyed wanted to see him in the job.
Schroeder, a more dynamic and moderate figure, wins praise from CDU voters but his party puts them off.

"The same people who want to have him as chancellor think the SPD is politically incompetent," he said. "Only 15 percent of all voters and 23 percent of those who prefer Schroeder to Kohl trust the SPD to handle the problems facing Germany."
Guellner said Forsa polls showed only 30 percent of all voters thought the SPD could win in 1998. Even among SPD voters, only 42 percent thought Kohl could be defeated.
Of the voters from either party who prefer Schroeder to Kohl, only 39 percent of them thought the SPD could win.
